title: The Authority of the Text
text:
Literary criticism has long oscillated between the claim that a text possesses an autonomous, self-sufficient meaning and the counter-claim that every reading is inevitably mediated by the interpretive frameworks of its reader. The New Critics, for instance, insisted that the poem itself, rather than the poet's biography or intentions, should be the sole object of analysis. Post-structuralist thinkers subsequently dismantled this confidence, arguing that language is inherently unstable and that meaning is deferred rather than fixed. Such debates are not merely academic, since they determine whether a canon is regarded as a natural reflection of excellence or as an ideological construction.

Reader-response theory shifted attention toward the act of reading itself, locating meaning in the encounter between text and reader. Critics such as Stanley Fish argued that interpretive communities, rather than individual readers, stabilise what a text is taken to mean. Yet this relocation of authority has been criticised for flattening the distinction between a careful interpretation and an arbitrary one. The tension, in the end, is productive: it compels critics to justify their claims rather than simply assert them.

questions.text: According to the passage, what did the New Critics insist should be the sole object of analysis?
options: The historical period in which the poem was written
The reader's emotional response to the poem
The poem itself, rather than the poet's biography or intentions
The canon of accepted literary masterpieces

questions.text: According to the passage, what has been the main criticism of the shift toward the reader?
options: It focuses exclusively on the author's biography
It denies that texts have any linguistic structure
It makes no clear distinction between careful and arbitrary interpretation
It rejects the idea of interpretive communities

questions.text: What can be inferred about the author's view of canon formation?
options: The author believes canon formation is settled by objective literary merit alone
The author treats canon formation as a question that remains contested
The author thinks canons are irrelevant to academic study
The author argues that canons are formed entirely by publishers

questions.text: Which claim is most consistent with the passage's view of critical argument?
options: Interpretation is a purely private act requiring no justification
Critics should avoid theoretical frameworks altogether
Meaning is fixed once the author has finished writing
Interpretations should be justified rather than merely asserted

paragraph_translations: La crítica literaria ha oscilado durante mucho tiempo entre la afirmación de que un texto posee un significado autónomo y autosuficiente y la contraafirmación de que toda lectura está inevitablemente mediada por los marcos interpretativos de su lector. Los Nuevos Críticos, por ejemplo, insistían en que el poema en sí, y no la biografía o las intenciones del poeta, debía ser el único objeto de análisis. Posteriormente, los pensadores posestructuralistas desmantelaron esta confianza, argumentando que el lenguaje es inherentemente inestable y que el significado se aplaza en lugar de fijarse. Estos debates no son meramente académicos, ya que determinan si un canon se considera un reflejo natural de la excelencia o una construcción ideológica.

La teoría de la recepción desplazó la atención hacia el acto mismo de leer, situando el significado en el encuentro entre texto y lector. Críticos como Stanley Fish sostuvieron que las comunidades interpretativas, y no los lectores individuales, estabilizan lo que se entiende que un texto significa. Sin embargo, este desplazamiento de la autoridad ha sido criticado por difuminar la distinción entre una interpretación cuidadosa y una arbitraria. En última instancia, la tensión es productiva: obliga a los críticos a justificar sus afirmaciones en lugar de limitarse a enunciarlas.
